resource_estimate.method: Per-row on-disk byte cost measured from the M01_COHORT_TRAIN and M02_VALIDATION_WARM parquet files already on the server (du -b), scaled linearly by the target manifests' sourced row counts. Peak RSS is scaled from company/handoffs/DATA-04.md's single measured BUILD_ALL peak (5,423 MiB). All scaling below is INFERENCE / derived_at_build (assumes near-linear behavior); no direct measurement of the addendum builder exists, because nothing is built by this task.

M_FULL_TRAIN_disk_estimate.flag: derived_at_build (INFERENCE: linear per-row scaling from measured M01 sizes)

M_FULL_VALIDATION_WARM_disk_estimate.row_count_estimation_note: The exact full decisions/users row counts (incl. censored) are not in any source (see manifests[1].expected_counts.n_decisions above). For SIZING ONLY (not a manifest expected_count) they are approximated by applying M02's censored/non-E2E density ratios to the sourced E2E figures: decisions ~= (1000189/808610) * 8430391 ~= 10,427,752 rows; users ~= (81086/62368) * 642228 ~= 834,975 rows. This approximation is INFERENCE, kept separate from the manifest's own expected_counts.

cross_check.method: DATA-04's 8 pre-lock manifests totalled 211.8 MB on disk (company/handoffs/DATA-04.md L86-88) for 9,927,869 total decision/query rows (sum of the 8 manifests' decisions/queries counts, company/handoffs/DATA-04.md L124-131). The new two manifests add an estimated ~50,608,360 such rows (40,180,608 + ~10,427,752), a 5.098x row-count ratio. 211.8 MB * 5.098 = 1.006 GiB, consistent with the 0.976 GiB bottom-up estimate.

rss_estimate.worst_case_scale_factor: 10.2844x (M_FULL_TRAIN's own decisions-row scale factor alone, i.e. assuming the single largest manifest's build dominates peak RSS as if its whole decisions table were materialized in memory at once)
rss_estimate.verdict: CENTRAL ESTIMATE FEASIBLE (about 37 GiB of margin under the 64 GiB cgroup). WORST-CASE ESTIMATE MARGINAL (about 9-10 GiB of margin). Both figures are INFERENCE / derived_at_build scaling from a single prior measurement (DATA-04's one BUILD_ALL run covering 8 much smaller manifests); the addendum builder's actual memory behavior under a roughly 10x population increase is unmeasured.
rss_estimate.recommendation: OPEN POINT FOR FABLE: run the addendum builder once under an RSS guard (as company/handoffs/DATA-04.md's run_bounded.py) with a hard cap well below 64 GiB (e.g. 24-32 GiB) before the real tie-break launch, and build the two manifests in separate passes rather than concurrently if the guard is approached, to keep peak RSS closer to the central estimate than the worst case.
